The application permits side access for a docking tool and a rear service port. The mechanical comparator receives the same access.

A paid external support captures the moving assembly before release. Alignment clamps and temporary stops are removed before the passive hold. There is no permanent fastener bypassing the copper seams.

Receiver architecture
Part	Proposed construction
Structural carriers	Two 50 × 50 mm, 8 mm-thick machined steel carriers; four mounting ports per face
Contact array	100 islands in a 10 × 10 array, 4.5 mm pitch
Contact island	2 × 2 mm, supported by four folded spring links
Spring links	17-7PH steel, 0.30 mm wide × 0.40 mm thick; two 1 mm legs per link
Active terminals	160 nickel ribs per island, 20 µm high, with 1.8 mm × 5 µm exposed tips
Protective system	Approximately 1 µm Parylene-C on sidewalls and surrounding surfaces; approximately 100 nm Ir on exposed tips
Joining separation	Nominally 3 µm
Useful copper section	144 mm² summed over all ribbons
Counterelectrode	10 cm² of 35 µm Cu foil, patterned into recessed intertile gutters and electrically insulated from the working faces
Working fluid	10 mL of 0.5 M CuSO₄ and 1.0 M H₃PO₄
Complete package	Approximately 28 mm thick, including spring layers, manifolds, seals and cartridge

The working surface is therefore a prepared Ni/Ir-coated spring-island receiver. Its coating, carrier, electrical connection and manufacture are included.

The counterelectrode remains recessed and mechanically separate. An accidental counterelectrode connection would be a short or an unintended load path, not useful seam strength.

Manufacture and preparation

The spring sheet is cut, aged, attached and inspected before depositing the fragile protective layers. Commercial 17-7PH strip covers the selected thickness. Supplier strength figures are typical v
